title: Telegram Bot API Python: Free Tools, Real Trade-offs
meta_description: What does Telegram Bot API Python cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and honest…
intro: Let's be honest: the internet is full of posts that pretend telegram bot api python is complicated. It isn't. What's actually complicated is separating the free options that hold up from the free options that quietly become $20/month. That's what this post digs into.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Sqlite, Open-meteo Weather API, and Polite Scraping — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

In practice that means: Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Sqlite
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: SQLite is the most deployed database in the world — free, public domain, and a single file.

In other words: For a self-hosted stack it removes an entire class of infrastructure: no server process, no connection pool, no backup job (copy the file). Full-text search is built in, which is plenty for a personal content database.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.

sections.heading: Open-meteo Weather API
paragraphs: Start with the basics. Open-Meteo is a free weather API with no API key, no signup and generous call limits.

In practice that means: A single GET request returns forecast and historical data as JSON, and the non-commercial tier is free forever. It is the default answer to 'free weather api' precisely because it removes every friction step: no key, no billing, no trial.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
bullets: Call /v1/forecast with latitude, longitude and the variables you need
Parse the JSON response directly into your app
Cache the response — the data changes on a forecast horizon, not per request

sections.heading: Polite Scraping
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: The difference between 'scraping' and 'being blocked' is politeness: identify yourself, rate-limit, and cache.

In other words: A descriptive User-Agent, a few seconds between requests, honoring robots.txt, and caching responses are the whole etiquette. Most sites allow reasonable personal-use access; the keyless endpoints this engine uses are the same ones the search boxes use, and they reward clients who behave.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.
bullets: Set a descriptive User-Agent with contact info
Space requests (this engine sleeps between outbound calls)
Cache results per query — never re-fetch what you already have
